findings.claim: The R7 ceiling move (CI fast 90->125, invariant 20->25) reached the workflow, ADR-019 section 5, ADR-029 section 2 and README's table, but NOT the documents of record that publish the ruling — four surviving sentences state a CI ceiling of 90/20 or assert CI has never measured this tree, and one contradicts its own document two sections later.
findings.evidence: ADR-029:6 (**Ruling**) reads "CI's `EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_FAST` **stays at 90** because nothing in this change measured CI" while :70 of the same file is headed "### 2. CI has measured this tree, and both its ceilings are derived from that". ADR-019:6 (**Ruling**) reads "CI `fast` 80 -> **90s**, CI `invariant` **20s**" while :387 is headed "### 5. CI's two numbers, measured on CI: 125 and 25". ADR-019:63-66 is flatly false as written ("measurements of a SMALLER tree than the one shipping ... CI's committed 90s ceiling is a number no run of this tree has tested") — section 5 now records 14a6a7b at 213 fast / 74 invariant, this tree exactly. ADR-019:10 (**Amended by**) repeats "CI's stays 90". INDEX.md:38 — the file whose own header says it is read "when you just need 'what is now true'" — publishes "stays 90 ... CI is expected to breach on this branch". Ground truth: .github/workflows/eval.yml:39-40 declares 125 and 25. Nothing grades any of these five locations. Confirmed independently by the orchestrator, including that CI run 32939583133 on e0ea784 now passes under the derived ceilings.
findings.acceptance: ADR-019:6, ADR-019:10, ADR-029:6 and INDEX.md:38 state CI's ceilings as 125s/25s derived from run 32937020758, and ADR-019:63-74's 'smaller tree / unmeasured / local-only' paragraph is struck in place with a dated pointer the way section 5's two retired paragraphs were. Ideally the CI ceilings in the Ruling headers and INDEX are read back from .github/workflows/eval.yml by `ci-numbers-are-derived` (it already parses that file), watched red first.

findings.claim: This diff overturns ADR-021's explicit CI ruling without recording the supersession anywhere, and ADR-021 carries no `Amended by` line at all — so the ADR chain still presents 'EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_FAST stays 90 and _INVARIANT stays 20' as the ruled state.
findings.evidence: ADR-021:115 is headed "### The ceiling stays at 90, and that is a ruling"; :133 states "`EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_FAST` stays 90 and `_INVARIANT` stays 20. That is now the ruled state rather than the untouched default"; :42 repeats it. The header block (:6-11) has Ruling/Because/Enforced by/Amends and no **Amended by** — compare ADR-019:10, which carries one. ADR-029's Amends line names only 'ADR-019 Decision 2', so nothing records that ADR-021's CI ruling was superseded on 2026-08-26. INDEX.md:30 also still says "CI's `EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_FAST` stays 90 and that is a RULING, not a deferral".
findings.acceptance: ADR-021 gains an `**Amended by**` line naming the ADR that moved CI's two ceilings off 90/20, its :115/:133/:42 'stays 90' sentences are struck in place with a dated pointer, and INDEX.md:30 no longer presents 'CI's fast stays 90' as a live ruling.

findings.claim: `adr029-variance-cites-the-ledger`, which this diff newly promotes to 'what keeps this section from acquiring such a literal again', does not redden on a wall-clock literal that ends a sentence — the exact shape of the original defect it was written for.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:5318 uses `(?<![\d.])(\d+\.\d+)s(?![\d.])`; the trailing negative lookahead rejects a match whose next character is `.`, so a sentence-ending literal is invisible. ADR-029:44 now claims the check is what keeps section 1 from acquiring a literal again, while section 1 carries none (`got.quoted == []`), making the guard the only thing standing there. Demonstrated: injecting "The band was 91.23s and that is the spread." -> passed False, quoted [91.23] (correctly red); "The band was 91.23s." -> passed True, quoted [] (green, WRONG — 91.23 is in no ledger row).
findings.repro: Inject a sentence-final seconds literal into ADR-029 section 1 and call `_check_adr029_variance_cites_the_ledger()` — returns passed True with quoted [].
findings.acceptance: The literal regex matches a seconds figure regardless of following punctuation (e.g. lookahead `(?!\d)`), the sentence-final injection is watched red before the change, and the mid-sentence and struck-span behaviours are unchanged (`~~...~~` still exempt, `105s`-style integers still exempt).
